doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Phil Schaap radio interview in a snowstorm
summary: Bauer recalls a marathon radio interview with Phil Schaap that ran for hours during a snowstorm.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well let me move up a few years.
I know, I’ll never get through it.
I went on one of these interviews by radio, and oddly enough it was a snow storm, just like today. But I’m there and there’s Phil Schaap.

Yeah, he’s interviewing. And it was supposed to be for an hour. And we’re talking and talking, and all of a sudden it’s three hours. And my wife is out there. She come back, she says, “It’s snowing.” So I says to Phil, “I’d better go.” He says, “Yeah, well right after this.” And then we go on. So it got so bad, he says, “You’ve only got a little while longer, © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
you know” and then we go on for another three hours. So in the middle of the program, well it wasn’t the middle, I says, “Phil, it’s snowing outside. See you.”

And I went out on the radio in the car and I put the program on, and I was still on, only my records. He was playing “The Way You Look,” he had all the outtakes. No but my mouth, I can’t stop talking.
